collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: The eldest council member seems to fall asleep during a long dispute: carry on talking, or wake them gently.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) and (neighbor), a neighbor, have brought a dispute about a shared ladder to the elders. (subject), the eldest on the council, appears to have fallen asleep partway through the very long explanation. (neighbor) has stopped talking and is looking at (subject) pointedly. (friend) isn't sure whether to carry on.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) carries on. (subject) doesn't stir. At the end there is a long silence. Then (subject) opens one eye and says, "The ladder's been borrowed four times this season, and three times it came back with a broken rung. Mend the rung, both of you, and leave the ladder at the meeting place for anyone." Nobody knows how (subject.he/she) heard. Nobody asks.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) touches (subject)'s arm. (subject) wakes, looks round, and says, "I'm sorry. Could you tell it again? Shorter, this time?" (friend) tells it again, very short. It turns out to be a very small dispute, told short. (subject) settles it in three sentences, and everyone goes home earlier than they expected.
